import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Cuban Primes

OEIS A002407 lists the primes that are differences of two consecutive positive cubes. The
sequence is conjectured to be infinite.

*References:*
- [OEIS A002407](https://oeis.org/A002407)
-/

namespace OeisA2407

/-- A natural number is in A002407 when it is prime and is the difference of two consecutive
positive cubes. The addition equality avoids truncated subtraction in `ℕ`. -/
def A (p : ℕ) : Prop :=
  p.Prime ∧ ∃ k > 0, p + k ^ 3 = (k + 1) ^ 3

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_7 : A 7 := by
  refine ⟨by norm_num, 1, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_19 : A 19 := by
  refine ⟨by norm_num, 2, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_37 : A 37 := by
  refine ⟨by norm_num, 3, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_61 : A 61 := by
  refine ⟨by norm_num, 4, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_127 : A 127 := by
  refine ⟨by norm_num, 6, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem not_a_91 : ¬ A 91 := by
  norm_num [A, Nat.prime_def_lt]

/--
This sequence is believed to be infinite.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture : {p : ℕ | A p}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end OeisA2407

reformulations.difference: Lean uses the natural-number equation p + k^3 = (k + 1)^3 with k > 0, instead of subtraction or OEIS's equivalent characterization p = 1 + 3k(k + 1).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Expanding (k + 1)^3 gives k^3 + 1 + 3k(k + 1), so the additive equation and the difference-of-cubes condition are exactly equivalent to the quadratic formula. Allowing k = 0 adds only p = 1, which primality excludes. Both the predicate equivalences and the resulting equivalence of infinitude statements were proved in the scratch file without using the conjecture.

sources_consulted: OEIS A002407, complete entry (revision #214, June 28, 2026), read via https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A002/A002407.seq; the canonical https://oeis.org/A002407 endpoint was blocked by Cloudflare.
review.notes: Checked all eight declarations. The five positive membership tests agree with OEIS, and 91 = 6^3 − 5^3 is correctly rejected because it is composite. Scratch proofs establish that every member is at least 7 and give an exact computable bounded-search characterization. Evaluation checked all p < 1000 and reproduced all 44 terms displayed in the OEIS entry. The six existing test proofs and the scratch equivalence proofs contain no sorry dependency. OEIS still records 'This sequence is believed to be infinite,' consistent with the research open tag. Experiments compile in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.
